label: Person
name: Orodes IV of Elymais
summary:
Orodes IV of Elymais (fl. 2nd century CE) was the ruler of Elymais, a region on the Persian border, from approximately 200 to 202 CE.

He may be the same Orodes mentioned in the inscriptions of the Tang-e Sarvak site, a archaeological discovery that sheds light on the pre-Islamic history of the region. This inscription suggests Orodes IV's involvement with the Parthian Empire and his attempts to maintain Elymais' independence in the face of Roman expansion.

Orodes IV's significance lies in his role as a regional leader during a time of great turmoil, as the Roman Empire expanded its borders and the Parthian Empire declined. His actions, or lack thereof, had a profound impact on the region's politics and geography.

The legacy of Orodes IV can be seen in the continued presence of Elymais in the region until the 7th century CE, when it was conquered by the Arabs.

The annual rainfall in Elymais has been recorded as low as 50 mm during his reign, highlighting the devastating effects of climate change on the region's agricultural productivity.

As the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus noted, 'Orodes IV was a man of great courage and strength, but also of little wisdom.'
